title: Pixel Parable
style: Pixel art: 8-bit characters built from square pixels (no anti-aliasing: snap every pixel to a 6 px grid) stand on a dark ground strip under a pale sky. A cautionary tale told with pixel props, a swarm of notification icons, and a pixel serpent that coils along a path. A few crisp UI cards (not pixelated) cut in to show numbers. Captions are serif word ladders (kit captions.ts): short stacks of mixed sizes, one key word in the accent italic, set beside the action and arriving word by word.
learnsFrom: Founder explainer reels (Instagram, @gregisenberg's team): 8-bit characters at desks on a ground strip, pixel buildings, a swarm of notification icons, a pixel snake on a path, a grid of icons flipping colour, clean UI cards cut into pixel scenes.

story.what: hook: a pixel manager stands before a team of three at desks; caption 'We rewarded meetings booked.'
the team books meetings: calendar icons pop out of their desks in a growing swarm; a counter card ticks 12 → 240
the calendar tower wobbles: a grid of meeting icons flips from teal to magenta one by one ('no-shows'); caption 'so they booked everything'
a pixel serpent slides along a path through the office, eating the day; caption 'The metric became the goal.'
the fix: a UI card shows two metrics side by side ('meetings held' and 'decisions made'), both sparklines rise; the icons flip back to teal
sign-off: the team high-fives in pixels; 'Oriel' pixel sign rises; caption 'measure the outcome, not the count'

sizes: Landscape widens the office so the team and the manager share one frame; captions sit top left.
sound: beatScore drive at 120 bpm, 8-bit flavoured (bright plucks), ticks for every icon pop, a hit when the serpent appears and the sign-off.
teaches: Pixel art is a grid decision: snap everything to one pixel size and the style holds, even when crisp UI cuts in.
